research:
I've gathered the data needed. Below is what was available as of 2026-10-01.

## 1. Resolution source
- The question resolves on FRED series CCNSA, which comes from DOL's weekly "Unemployment Insurance Weekly Claims" release. The first value for the week ending 2026-09-26 will be the advance NSA insured unemployment figure in the DOL release of Thursday 2026-10-08. [FRED CCNSA](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/CCNSA)
- 2026-10-01: The latest DOL release shows advance NSA insured unemployment (state programs) of **1,498,378** for the week ending 2026-09-19. A later DOL table revises this slightly, to about 1,497,2xx. [DOL release](https://www.dol.gov/sites/dolgov/files/OPA/newsreleases/ui-claims/20261543.pdf)
- The week ending 2026-09-12 was first printed at 1,552,283 (the code baseline), and has since been revised a few thousand lower.
- NSA advance figures are usually revised by only a few thousand the next week. That doesn't matter here, because the question uses the first print.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. The value for the week ending 9/26 is not published until 2026-10-08.
- The last known point is already about 54,000 below the 9/12 print. The series is in its usual seasonal decline from the July peak (about 1.85M).

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-10-01: Initial claims came in at 197K seasonally adjusted (SA) against 200K expected, with the prior week revised to 198K. The 4-week average is 200.0K. SA continuing claims were **1.701M** against 1.725M expected, down from 1.719M (week ending 9/19). [investingLive](https://investinglive.com/news/us-weekly-initial-jobless-claims-197k-vs-200k-expected/)
- 2026-10-01: Coverage describes SA continuing claims as the lowest since March 2023, and initial claims as near 57-year lows. The low was 189K in mid-July, the lowest since 1969. [MarketReview](https://www.marketreview.com/news/us-jobless-claims-197000-continuing-claims/), [TheStreet](https://pro.thestreet.com/market-commentary/initial-jobless-claims-remain-near-57-year-lows-continuing-claims-a-3-year-low)
- 2026-09-25: The previous release had initial claims at 197K (week ending 9/19), described as near a 57-year low. [Yahoo/Reuters](https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/articles/u-jobless-claims-fall-197-112500927.html), [Quartz](https://qz.com/us-jobless-claims-197000-57-year-low-092526)
- Week ending 9/19: NSA initial claims were 163,811, up 6.7% from the week before.

## 4. Base rates
Recent NSA path in 2026 (FRED; values may include revisions):
- 8/22: 1,734,461
- 8/29: 1,668,037
- 9/5: 1,565,675
- 9/12: about 1.55M
- 9/19: 1,498,378 (advance)

The weekly drops are shrinking (-102K, -20K, -48K), which fits the end of the summer-to-fall decline.

Seasonal move from the week ending around 9/19 to the week ending around 9/26 (FRED, revised values):

| Year | ~9/19 | ~9/26 | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2025 | 1,696,023 | 1,683,703 | -0.7% |
| 2024 | 1,613,719 | 1,614,385 | +0.0% |
| 2023 | 1,588,285 | 1,585,277 | -0.2% |
| 2022 | 1,217,825 | 1,233,270 | +1.3% |
| 2021 | 2,469,313 | 2,395,401 | -3.0% (pandemic unwind, not typical) |

- In the normal years (2022 to 2025), the one-week change ran from -0.7% to +1.3%, with a median near 0%. Applied to the 1,498,378 advance print, that gives roughly **1.488M to 1.518M**, centered near 1.495M to 1.50M.
- The first print for the target week is an advance estimate. Its gap from the revised value is usually a few thousand, which is small next to the seasonal spread.
- This year is running well below recent years: about 198K (12%) below the same week of 2025, and about 115K below 2024. That matches SA continued claims at a 3-year low.
- The code baseline (two steps ahead from 9/12, median about 1.532M) is now out of date. With the 9/19 print in, only one week remains, and history points to a much tighter range around 1.50M.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold market on NSA continued claims.
- Consensus forecasts cover only the SA series. For the week ending 9/19, consensus was 1.725M and the actual was 1.701M. I couldn't find a published consensus for SA continuing claims for the week ending 9/26 as of 10/01.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- 2026-10-08, 8:30 ET: The DOL weekly claims release publishes the advance NSA continued claims for the week ending 9/26. This is the resolution value.
- The week ending 9/26 has no holiday or calendar quirk; Columbus Day falls in October, after the target week. Weather isn't a driver here, and I found no major hurricane or disaster claims flagged for late September.
- If a federal government shutdown or lapse in funding happened, it could delay publication. I found no such disruption reported as of 10/01.
